designPlan.artDirection: A premium fantasy-tech main menu centered on a luminous AURORA title plate and a dominant Play button, using a tightly controlled glossy cyan and cobalt palette with thick navy structural edging and warm gold highlight trim. The background stays mostly native and restrained: a deep desaturated blue field with subtle vertical glow falloff, faint radial cyan bloom behind the title/button stack, and four small ornamental corner image details that frame rather than fill the screen. Generated artwork is reserved for the title plate, button skins, panel skins, and icon family so the screen feels cohesive without becoming noisy. Text remains live, bright, and highly legible over darker glossy surfaces. Settings and Credits open modal panels that inherit the same skin language, while the Music toggle and Volume slider are fully native controls styled with gradients, rounded tracks, thick outlines, and gold-active accents instead of baked artwork.

composition.focalPoint: The main focal point is a vertical central stack: ornate AURORA title plate above a large unmistakable Play CTA, followed by two smaller peer actions for Settings and Credits. Secondary focus shifts to centered modals that overlay the stack without changing the screen’s overall symmetry. Decorative corners and background glow support this axis but never compete with it.
secondaryRegions: top_title frames the composition with the title plate and live AURORA heading.
modal_settings appears centered above the menu for interactive audio settings.
modal_credits appears centered above the menu as a smaller informational panel.
corner_ornaments lightly anchor the four screen corners with restrained matching detail.
background_base provides dark atmospheric contrast and subtle cyan bloom behind the center stack.
composition.alignmentSystem: Strong vertical center alignment on desktop and mobile, with shared widths and even button rhythm. Comparable actions live in a single dock/list. Panels are center anchored and internally left-aligned for form readability, while their close buttons remain top-right aligned. Ornamentation mirrors across corners for balance. All major elements snap to a 4/8/16 spacing cadence with consistent internal padding and equal edge treatment.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt carry the glossy fantasy-tech identity, deep navy supplies thick structural separation and readable edge contrast, and warm gold is used sparingly for highlights, active emphasis, and ornamental trim. Text stays near-white with a softer blue secondary tone to preserve clarity over saturated surfaces. Success and danger exist only as semantic utility colors for toggle state feedback, without implying extra systems.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outlines on primary surfaces, generally 3px equivalent for buttons and 2px for inner control framing, with selective gold inner strokes or top-edge sheen for premium polish. Text is not heavily outlined; readability comes from contrast, subtle shadow, and clean placement.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Medium-depth cool shadows with short offset and soft blur under actionable surfaces, plus a restrained cyan bloom behind the central stack and faint panel lift shadow for modals. Shadows separate layers without muddying the glossy colors.

display.treatment: Used only for the AURORA title text over the title plate, uppercase with slight tracking, bright near-white fill, and a subtle navy shadow for separation.

heading.treatment: Panel titles and key section headings; crisp, high-contrast, no heavy outline, slight letter spacing.

button.treatment: Centered live labels with strong readability, modest tracking, bright fill, and minimal shadow; Play can run slightly larger than peer secondary buttons.

body.treatment: Settings labels and credits body text; calm, readable, and slightly cool-toned secondary text where hierarchy demands.

caption.treatment: Used sparingly for compact helper/value text, maintaining contrast and uncluttered spacing.

numeric.treatment: Volume value text aligned with slider, tabular-feeling spacing via consistent container width rather than stylized treatment.

badge.treatment: Reserved for tiny ornamental labels only if needed; no extra badge systems are introduced.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Generated cohesive icon family for play, settings, credits, and close using glossy cyan/cobalt enamel shapes with warm gold highlight cuts and thick navy edging to match the button skins.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use a unified premium response: buttons and close actions lift slightly, gain brighter top sheen, and deepen shadow; toggle and slider increase localized glow only. Modals do not wobble or float continuously.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls compress briefly with eased snap, preserving a firm tactile feel. Toggle thumb shifts with a quick eased slide; slider handle enlarges subtly while dragging.
motionSystem.entrance: Initial menu enters with a short upward fade for title and dock together, followed by a slightly delayed sheen settle. Modals scale from 0.96 to 1 with fade when opened and reverse cleanly when closed.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls to their resting scale and shadow in a quick, polished ease-out without bounce exaggeration.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Reduce to opacity and minimal color/outline transitions only; disable sheen sweeps, vertical drift, and scale amplification while preserving state clarity.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag feedback only; no synthetic hover. Press feedback is immediate and readable, and modal transitions remain short to avoid sluggishness.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI hover or click sounds are emitted on touch or pointer because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a downstream implementation attempts to add audio, it should report unresolved audio semantics rather than fabricate asset IDs.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered vertical composition: title plate near the upper third, then the button stack below. Settings and Credits modals appear as centered overlays sized for mouse readability, with rows staying horizontal and compact. Decorative corners may be slightly more pronounced than mobile but remain peripheral.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Widen the action dock substantially, reduce ornamental footprint, and keep the title plate slightly higher with more vertical compression. Buttons remain large and thumb-safe. Settings modal becomes wider and taller with touch-friendly row spacing and enlarged slider/toggle hit areas. Credits modal also widens for readability. Preserve the dominant Play hierarchy.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile structural group when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600; otherwise tablet can retain the desktop grouping but with moderated widths between phone and desktop. Increase central stack width compared with full desktop and keep modals comfortably sized for touch plus pointer use.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing the same semantic nodeNames from the supported library structure; desktop visible initially.

Keep exact node names from libraryTemplate: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, MusicRow, VolumeRow, SettingsCloseButton, CreditsModal, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add shop, rewards, currency, ranks, quests, tabs, inventory, extra navigation, or any other product systems.

Use generated artwork only for button skins, panel skins, title plate, corner ornaments, and the play/settings/credits/close icon family. Keep MusicToggle and VolumeSlider fully native Roblox controls styled through Frame, UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, and property animation.

Because the supported structure omits separate MusicToggle and VolumeSlider node names, implement them as the real interactive controls inside MusicRow and VolumeRow while binding the requirement IDs to those rows’ actionable components.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal should start hidden/inactive and be shown by the actual controller, not just mocked visually.
PanelControllerBehavior should manage mutually exclusive modal visibility, dim/input-block overlay if used, close actions, and menu dismissal on Play.
On Play, fire a clearly named local integration event/hook from OnPlayRequestedHook such as OnPlayRequested, then trigger close_main_menu behavior to hide the main menu.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated visual construction; route button interactions through a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating code per button.
Close buttons share one skin and one generated close icon. Settings and Credits main menu buttons share the same secondary button skin. Both modals share the same panel skin.
Keep text live for all labels, titles, settings labels, any credits copy, and volume value. Do not bake text into artwork.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on title and buttons to avoid overflow across aspect ratios. Use UIAspectRatioConstraint for the title plate and optional corner ornament images.
Use CanvasGroup for modal fade transitions if available; otherwise animate transparency consistently across modal children.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Since sounds were not requested, leave hover/click sounds disabled.
Runtime viewport selection must switch to mobile layout when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600 without depending on Controller execution inside the renderer.

iconSystem.styleDescription: Generated cohesive icon family for play, settings, credits, and close using glossy cyan/cobalt enamel shapes with warm gold highlight cuts and thick navy edging to match the button skins.

motionSystem.hover: Pointer-capable devices use a unified premium response: buttons and close actions lift slightly, gain brighter top sheen, and deepen shadow; toggle and slider increase localized glow only. Modals do not wobble or float continuously.
motionSystem.press: All actionable controls compress briefly with eased snap, preserving a firm tactile feel. Toggle thumb shifts with a quick eased slide; slider handle enlarges subtly while dragging.
motionSystem.entrance: Initial menu enters with a short upward fade for title and dock together, followed by a slightly delayed sheen settle. Modals scale from 0.96 to 1 with fade when opened and reverse cleanly when closed.
motionSystem.release: Release returns controls to their resting scale and shadow in a quick, polished ease-out without bounce exaggeration.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: Reduce to opacity and minimal color/outline transitions only; disable sheen sweeps, vertical drift, and scale amplification while preserving state clarity.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag feedback only; no synthetic hover. Press feedback is immediate and readable, and modal transitions remain short to avoid sluggishness.

audioSystem.touchBehavior: No UI hover or click sounds are emitted on touch or pointer because sounds were not requested.
audioSystem.fallbackBehavior: If a downstream implementation attempts to add audio, it should report unresolved audio semantics rather than fabricate asset IDs.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build _NexusDesktop with a centered vertical composition: title plate near the upper third, then the button stack below. Settings and Credits modals appear as centered overlays sized for mouse readability, with rows staying horizontal and compact. Decorative corners may be slightly more pronounced than mobile but remain peripheral.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build _NexusMobile independently rather than scaling desktop. Widen the action dock substantially, reduce ornamental footprint, and keep the title plate slightly higher with more vertical compression. Buttons remain large and thumb-safe. Settings modal becomes wider and taller with touch-friendly row spacing and enlarged slider/toggle hit areas. Credits modal also widens for readability. Preserve the dominant Play hierarchy.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile structural group when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600; otherwise tablet can retain the desktop grouping but with moderated widths between phone and desktop. Increase central stack width compared with full desktop and keep modals comfortably sized for touch plus pointer use.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frame groups at View.build() return, each containing the same semantic nodeNames from the supported library structure; desktop visible initially.

Keep exact node names from libraryTemplate: BackgroundRoot, BackgroundOrnaments, MainMenuDock, TitlePlate, AuroraTitle, PlayButton, SettingsButton, CreditsButton, SettingsModal, MusicRow, VolumeRow, SettingsCloseButton, CreditsModal, CreditsCloseButton, OnPlayRequestedHook, PanelControllerBehavior.
Do not add shop, rewards, currency, ranks, quests, tabs, inventory, extra navigation, or any other product systems.

Use generated artwork only for button skins, panel skins, title plate, corner ornaments, and the play/settings/credits/close icon family. Keep MusicToggle and VolumeSlider fully native Roblox controls styled through Frame, UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, and property animation.

Because the supported structure omits separate MusicToggle and VolumeSlider node names, implement them as the real interactive controls inside MusicRow and VolumeRow while binding the requirement IDs to those rows’ actionable components.
SettingsModal and CreditsModal should start hidden/inactive and be shown by the actual controller, not just mocked visually.
PanelControllerBehavior should manage mutually exclusive modal visibility, dim/input-block overlay if used, close actions, and menu dismissal on Play.
On Play, fire a clearly named local integration event/hook from OnPlayRequestedHook such as OnPlayRequested, then trigger close_main_menu behavior to hide the main menu.
Use local helper functions in View for repeated visual construction; route button interactions through a shared ButtonEffects module rather than duplicating code per button.
Close buttons share one skin and one generated close icon. Settings and Credits main menu buttons share the same secondary button skin. Both modals share the same panel skin.
Keep text live for all labels, titles, settings labels, any credits copy, and volume value. Do not bake text into artwork.
Use UITextSizeConstraint on title and buttons to avoid overflow across aspect ratios. Use UIAspectRatioConstraint for the title plate and optional corner ornament images.
Use CanvasGroup for modal fade transitions if available; otherwise animate transparency consistently across modal children.
No audio assets should be fabricated. Since sounds were not requested, leave hover/click sounds disabled.
Runtime viewport selection must switch to mobile layout when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600 without depending on Controller execution inside the renderer.

changeInstructions: Build a new main menu titled AURORA.
Include Play, Settings, and Credits actions.
Make Settings open a panel with Music on/off toggle and Volume slider.
Make Credits open a small panel.
Give both panels a Close action.
Ensure Play closes the menu and fires a clearly named local hook for game integration.
Support desktop and mobile layouts.
Use glossy cyan/cobalt artwork with thick navy edges, warm gold highlights, ornamental corner details, and a title plate.
Use Gemini-generated matching skins and icons for button skins, panel skin, title plate, ornamental details, and distinct play/settings/credits/close icons.
Implement coherent hover and press animation.
Use restrained native background layout.
Keep text live and readable.
Panels must open and close in the actual controller.
